definitions.explanation: A style, method, or design that follows Western (European/American) conventions, as opposed to traditional Japanese or Eastern styles.

examples.japanese: {洋式|ようしき}トイレを{使|つか}う。
この{建物|たてもの}は{洋式|ようしき}の{造|つく}りになっている。
examples.english: This building is built in Western style.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}に{日本|にほん}では{洋式|ようしき}の{生活|せいかつ}{様式|ようしき}が{広|ひろ}まった。
examples.english: Western lifestyles spread in Japan during the Meiji period.

notes:
Most commonly encountered in the phrase {洋式|ようしき}トイレ (Western-style toilet, i.e., a sit-down toilet), in contrast to {和式|わしき}トイレ (Japanese-style squat toilet). This distinction is very practical for learners in Japan, as signs in public restrooms often indicate the type available.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {洋式|ようしき}トイレ — Western-style (sit-down) toilet
- {洋式|ようしき}{建築|けんちく} — Western-style architecture
- {洋式|ようしき}の{部屋|へや} — Western-style room

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和式|わしき} — Japanese-style (the direct opposite)
- {様式|ようしき} — style, format (homophone with different kanji; refers to style or form in general)
